newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel survey finds economy slowing.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel survey finds economy slowing.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Monday that its survey of companies showed overall economic activity fell in the fourth quarter of 1996. It gave no specific figures.

"The response to the company survey conducted by the Bank of Israel for the fourth quarter of 1996 shows that the absence of growth in the economy that was registered from second quarter 1996 was substituted by a decline," the bank said.
The survey covered 650 industrial, building, trading and hotel companies.

The bank said industrial companies reported a decline in output for the first time since mass immigration to Israel from the former Soviet Union began in 1989. Building and hotel companies, which began reporting a decline in activity in the third quarter, said the trend had worsened in the fourth.

The survey also found that manufacturers' domestic sales fell in the quarter while exports were stable. However, makers of electronic and electrical goods and transport products reported higher output and exports. The responses were not adjusted for seasonal factors.

The Bank of Israel survey mirrors one conducted by the Manufactuers Association of 180 industrial companies that was released on Sunday. The Manufacturers' survey found that most industrial companies were expecting continued low levels of domestic sales in first-quarter 1997, with a slight improvement in exports.
